analysis.explanation: The Random Forest assigns a probability of only 0.60 to the malware class, which is a weak margin. Nearly all of the top-20 n-grams push toward cryptojacking (19 positive, 1 negative: XORPS LEA at -0.006155), but the individual contributions are small and spread out (+0.005 to +0.017), so no single feature is decisive. The strongest contributors are POP-initiated sequences (POP CALL +0.017296, POP XOR +0.014801, POP LEA +0.012102, POP PUSH +0.010953, POP TEST +0.010859, POP ADD +0.008112, POP MOV +0.005521). These reflect common function epilogue/prologue and calling-convention patterns, and they are generic to compiled code. They are not specific to mining. The more suggestive group is the SIMD/bit-manipulation family: MOVDQA MOVAPS (+0.010898), PAND PMOVMSKB (+0.008728), PXOR PXOR (+0.006520), PXOR MOVDQA (+0.005581), ROL MOV (+0.007819), MOV ROL (+0.007406), ROL AND (+0.005389) and XOR ADC (+0.005469). Rotates, XORs and vectorized register operations are consistent with hash or cipher computation of the kind used in proof-of-work algorithms. However, the same instructions also appear in legitimate cryptographic libraries, checksums, string routines (PAND/PMOVMSKB is a typical vectorized scan idiom) and compiler-optimized memory code. The evidence gives no function names, API calls, or per-function context, so these patterns cannot be tied to a mining loop. The frequencies are also low (mostly around 0.001 or less), which indicates no dominant computational kernel. The result is a modest lean toward cryptojacking that is inconclusive on its own.

key_indicators: Model probability of only 0.60 for malware, a marginal lean
19 of the top 20 n-grams push toward cryptojacking, but each contribution is small (max +0.0173)
Top-ranked features are generic POP-based stack/call sequences with low specificity
Rotate and XOR patterns (ROL MOV, MOV ROL, ROL AND, XOR ADC) are consistent with hash-like computation but ambiguous
SIMD patterns (PXOR PXOR, PXOR MOVDQA, MOVDQA MOVAPS, PAND PMOVMSKB) could reflect vectorized compute or standard optimized library code
XORPS LEA (-0.006155) provides a benign counter-signal
No function-level context or distinguishing evidence ties these patterns to a mining loop
analysis.recommended_action: Treat as inconclusive and escalate for further analysis rather than a verdict. Disassemble the functions containing the ROL/XOR/SIMD sequences and check whether they implement a known proof-of-work hash (e.g., CryptoNight, RandomX, or Ethash-style round structure) or a legitimate crypto/checksum routine. Run the sample in a sandbox to observe sustained CPU use, network connections to mining pools, and persistence behavior. Compare against known mining-family signatures and YARA rules before making a final determination.
